paper.title_en: Superorbital period evolution of Hercules X-1
paper.abstract_en: Context. Hercules X-1 (Her X-1) is a well-studied X-ray binary exhibiting superorbital modulation of its X-ray flux. The origin of this periodicity remains debated between a counter-precessing twisted-tilted accretion disc and free precession of the neutron star. Earlier observations (1970-1990) reported stochastic fluctuations in the superorbital period, with no long-term trend. Aims. We investigated the long-term trend of the superorbital modulation using more recent, uninterrupted data from 1995-2025 to identify features that may favour or disfavour the proposed mechanisms. Methods. We probed the superorbital period using long-term light curves from five X-ray monitors, namely CGRO/BATSE, RXTE/ASM, Swift/BAT, Fermi/GBM, and MAXI/GSC, together with literature data spanning $\sim$50 yr. We employed multiple timing analysis tools to trace its evolution. Results. The uninterrupted data from the last 30 years show that the superorbital period is decreasing at a rate of $\sim -5 \times 10^{-5}$ s s$^{-1}$. The $O-C$ analysis reveals shorter-timescale variability superimposed on the overall decay; thus, a simple quadratic function cannot explain the observed $O-C$ variations. We also find a positive correlation between the mean count rate and superorbital period across different linear segments of the $O-C$ curve. Conclusions. Period variations over a few to a few tens of superorbital cycles suggest a restoring mechanism in the system. We discuss possible mechanisms responsible for the observed long-term decay and short-term variability. (Abbreviated.)
